Synopsis:
    Climate warming is driving a structural shift in boreal forests from evergreen dominance (spruce, fir) toward deciduous tree species. Post-disturbance recovery (wildfires, storms), extended growing seasons and increased soil nitrogen all disproportionately favour deciduous trees. The transition is already observable in Alaska and Canada. Evergreens will persist but lose dominance, with downstream implications for carbon, water and energy cycles.
